output_json.patch_notes: PropertyClass.fromString() now: (1) returns null for null input, and (2) calls Class.forName(v, false, classLoader) with initialize=false, using the thread context classloader (falling back to the class's own classloader). This prevents execution of the named class's static initializer — the primary RCE vector for Class.forName on untrusted input — while preserving legitimate behavior, since the resolved Class object is only ever used for its name (asString() -> value.getName()) and is never instantiated by PropertyClass. Added regression test testPropertyClassDoesNotRunStaticInitializer() using a helper class whose static initializer flips a static flag; the test asserts the class is still resolved correctly but the initializer flag remains false. Full PropertyTest suite (33 tests) passes.
output_json.risk_notes: Low risk. Behavior for valid class names is unchanged aside from deferred static initialization; the loaded Class is only used for its name so no consumer relies on the class being initialized at resolution time. Uses the thread context classloader first to preserve resolvability in container/webapp environments, falling back to PropertyClass's own classloader. This blocks the static-initializer RCE path but does not add an allowlist, so class references can still be resolved (loaded, not initialized); if stricter policy is desired later, an allowlist of permitted classes could be layered on top. ClassNotFoundException still maps to IllegalArgumentException, so existing error-path tests are unaffected.
output_json.summary: Fixed a CWE-94 code-injection (RCE) in PropertyClass.fromString(), which called Class.forName(v) on an attacker-controllable class name reachable from deserialized/persisted property values (JSON/Mongo/etc.). Loading a class this way triggers its static initializer, enabling arbitrary code execution via gadget classes. The fix resolves the class without initializing it (Class.forName(v, false, classLoader)), blocking static-initializer execution while still returning the correct Class reference used only for its name.
